title: Sync batch
description: Entry point for the sync HTTP bodies. A document is exactly one of the three shapes; reference a specific one as batch.schema.json#/$defs/PushRequest, #/$defs/PushResponse or #/$defs/PullResponse. SYNC.md sections 5 and 6. Two lenient shapes say what a RECEIVER validates the whole body against: the server validates a push body against #/$defs/PushRequestLenient only (a mismatch is HTTP 400) and checks each op on its own, so a single op can be answered with unsupported_op or schema_invalid while the rest of the batch is processed; a client validates a pull body against #/$defs/PullResponseLenient and checks each op against op.schema.json only when it knows the op_type and op_version, so an old client applies the ops before the first unknown one and stops there (SYNC.md 6, 'upgrade required'). PushRequest and PullResponse are what a correct SENDER produces.

ops.description: Ops minted by ONE device (all device_id equal), in strictly ascending hlc. The server processes them in array order.

PushRequestLenient.title: PushRequestLenient
PushRequestLenient.description: What the server validates a push body against; the only whole-body check it may fail a push request on (HTTP 400). Everything stricter (op.schema.json, the envelope rules, the per-op checks of SYNC.md 5.3) is checked per op and reported as a 'rejected' result with unsupported_op, schema_invalid, ..., so one bad op never blocks the rest of the outbox. Duplicate keys (C-2, SYNC.md 5.2 'Parsing the body'): the server parses the body with a syntax-only, duplicate-tolerant parse. The body ALSO fails this shape (HTTP 400) if the top-level object repeats a key, if an element's op_id member is repeated, or if two elements have the same op_id with different contents. A duplicate key anywhere inside ops[i] is NOT a 400: that op is rejected with schema_invalid, decided before op_too_large. JSON Schema cannot express duplicate keys; these rules are normative text.

op_id.description: The op this result is for.

status.description: accepted: applied and logged now. duplicate: this op_id was already in the log; nothing was done. rejected: permanently refused; nothing was done.

seq.description: change.seq of the op. Present iff status is accepted or duplicate.

code.description: Machine-readable reason (SYNC.md section 5.3). Open set: clients treat an unknown code as a generic permanent rejection.

message.description: English diagnostic for logs and the sync-status screen; not for parsing.

PushResponse.title: PushResponse
PushResponse.description: Body of a successful POST /sync/push response.

results.description: Exactly one result per pushed op, in request order.

high_water_seq.description: Highest change.seq committed when the response was built; >= every seq in results. A client whose pull_seq is greater starts a log reset (SYNC.md 6.2); otherwise informational (pending pull count).

server_time.description: Server wall clock when the response was built; clients compare it with their own clock to warn about skew and to block minting when it exceeds 24 h (SYNC.md 3.4).

log_epoch.description: Identity of the server's log (SYNC.md 6.2). Changes only when the log is replaced (a restore from backup): seq values of different epochs are unrelated. A client that sees a value different from the one it stored starts a log reset.

durable_seq.description: Highest seq s such that every change row with seq <= s is in a verified backup that any restore will start from (SYNC.md 6.2). <= high_water_seq; never decreases within one log_epoch. A device keeps each acked pending_op row until acked_seq <= durable_seq.

ops.description: Log entries with seq > since, in strictly ascending seq, from every origin including the requester itself.

next_since.description: Cursor for the next pull: seq of the last op returned, or the request's since when ops is empty.

has_more.description: true = more ops exist after next_since; pull again immediately.

log_epoch.description: Identity of the server's log (SYNC.md 6.2). Changes only when the log is replaced (a restore from backup): seq values of different epochs are unrelated. A client that sees a value different from the one it stored starts a log reset.

durable_seq.description: Highest seq s such that every change row with seq <= s is in a verified backup that any restore will start from (SYNC.md 6.2). <= high_water_seq; never decreases within one log_epoch. A device keeps each acked pending_op row until acked_seq <= durable_seq.

PullResponseLenient.title: PullResponseLenient
PullResponseLenient.description: What a client validates a pull body against. Same as PullResponse, except that each op is only required to be an object with a known envelope shape and an open op_type / op_version: a client checks an op against op.schema.json only if it supports that op_type and op_version, and stops at the first op it does not support (SYNC.md 6). Unknown top-level properties are ignored, so the server may add some.

ops.description: Log entries with seq > since, in strictly ascending seq, from every origin including the requester itself.

op_type.description: May be a type this client does not know.

op_version.description: May be higher than this client supports.

next_since.description: Cursor for the next pull: seq of the last op returned, or the request's since when ops is empty.

has_more.description: true = more ops exist after next_since; pull again immediately.
